title: Voltstream SDK integration studio — auth + env walkthrough
summary: AE + SE walked Voltstream through Python/TypeScript SDK quickstart, auth patterns (API key, SSO/SAML, KMS), local dev env + sandbox, Console navigation and Redwood Optimize recommendations. Customer interested in Dedicated for P50 latency and VPC/KMS requirements. Agreed next step: provision sandbox keys, run end-to-end quickstart, schedule POC kickoff and perf baseline run.
next_steps: Maya to share sandbox credentials and quickstart repo link by 2025-10-22
Raj to provide performance checklist and sample perf test script
Voltstream to confirm POC target latency and sample dataset by 2025-10-27
Schedule POC kickoff (1 hour) for week of 2025-10-27
action_items: Owner: Maya Chen | Item: Share sandbox API keys + repo link | Due: 2025-10-22
Owner: Raj Patel | Item: Send perf checklist + load script | Due: 2025-10-22
Owner: Tom Alvarez | Item: Provide sample payload shapes and P50/P90 targets | Due: 2025-10-27
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-10-20 15:00 UTC | Duration: 42m | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Raj (Redwood SE), Anika (CTO), Tom (Eng Mgr), Priya (DevOps), Luis (Intern)

[00:00] Maya: okay hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm Maya from Redwood Inference, and with me is Raj on the engineer side. how's everyone doing?
[00:12] Anika: doing well, thanks. quick note, running a little late this morning so appreciate you fitting us in.
[00:18] Raj: no worries. quick agenda — we want to do a hands-on SDK quickstart in both python and typescript, show the console for routing and Optimize suggestions, and then talk auth/VPC/KMS needs for your compliance team. sound good?
[00:32] Tom: sounds great. our main goals are reliability and predictable latency. we're exploring hosted first but need to know what Dedicated/VPC would look like.
[00:43] Priya: and from infra, SSO + KMS are blockers for any pilot, so we need to see how credentials and rotation work.
[00:50] Maya: perfect, we'll hit those. okay Raj — quickstart.
[00:55] Raj: yep, i'm going to share my screen — starting with the repo layout. there's a py quickstart and a ts quickstart — both use the same underlying API. the python example shows pip install redwood-inference (note: package name is illustrative) and then set REDWOOD_API_KEY in env.
[01:18] Raj: (mumbles) i've seen teams do dotenv or k8s secrets for CI. the quickstart demonstrates a single request and streaming.
[01:27] Luis: small question — is the api key long-term? or do you recommend short lived tokens?
[01:32] Maya: we recommend short-lived tokens for prod. you can use static keys for dev/sandbox. For prod we integrate with customer KMS + our token service so keys rotate.
[01:44] Anika: can you show where the KMS integration happens? we use GCP KMS and have a rotation policy.
[01:50] Raj: sure — in the Console demo i'll show the key config. high-level: Redwood can accept wrapped keys via your KMS or you can bring-your-own-key to the private deployment. in hosted we have a connector that pulls from your KMS and rotates — there's metadata and audit records.
[02:08] Raj: i'm going to run the python quickstart now — a simple generate call, model is redwood-alpha-open (our catalog name, sometimes transcribed as redwood alpha open). run it..
[02:20] (typing)
[02:30] Raj: okay response streaming starts — you can see token-level timing in the console. that's useful to debug latency spikes.
[02:37] Tom: interesting, does streaming help with perceived latency vs end-to-end?
[02:41] Raj: yep — perceived latency improves. also we have prefix caching (k v cash in some notes) which saves repeated context.
[02:49] Priya: we've heard about KV cache but curious about cache invalidation and multi-tenant risks.
[02:56] Raj: good q. cache is per-tenant and per-model variant — invalidation hooks are available; you can TTL or clear via API. we can show the policy in the POC.
[03:12] Maya: quick pause — any procurement or compliance folks we should loop in now?
[03:17] Anika: i'll loop in security lead Sarah after this call.
[03:21] Maya: great. okay switching to typescript quickstart.
[03:25] Raj: ts example uses npm install @redwood/inference-client, env var REDWOOD_API_KEY or use the OIDC flow for SSO. here's a snippet that does a streaming prompt with function calling — note the function shape.
[03:40] Luis: i caught the phrase function calling — do you support structured outputs or function style return?
[03:45] Raj: yes both — structured outputs via JSON schema works well and function-calling is supported; it's super handy for tool orchestration.
[03:52] Anika: about VPC — if we go Dedicated, is there a path for private networking?
[03:58] Raj: Dedicated always supports VPC peering or customer VPC endpoints for private deployments. for on-prem we have an appliance option also.
[04:08] Tom: what's the SLA with Dedicated?
[04:11] Maya: SLA's are in the Dedicated contract — typically 99.9% with latency SLOs for P50/P95 at the committed capacity. we'll share specifics after this call.
[04:21] Maya: i want to demo the Console now — it's useful for both ops and devs.
[04:26] Raj: switching screens to Console. top left is project overview — token usage, cost breakdown by model, and a per-route latency chart. clicking into a route shows model pinned versions, rollout policy (canary, A/B), and fallback variants.
[04:45] Priya: can we set automatic fallback to a cheaper quantized model when load spikes?
[04:50] Raj: absolutely — routing policies let you tier by cost/latency and fallback to quantized variants. Redwood Optimize also suggests quantization profiles based on your observed workload. some notes show it as Redwood Optamize in the quick doc — ignore that typo.
[05:05] Tom: how do we validate quality regressions after a fallback?
[05:08] Raj: good point — Console has evals tied to prompt sets; when a fallback occurs you can run a post-check against the prompt set and alert on n-gram or embedding drift.
[05:22] Anika: about data retention and logs — we need full audit logs for requests and model versions for 1 year.
[05:30] Maya: hosted plan has configurable retention; for regulated customers Dedicated or Private deployments let you keep logs in your account and attach your SIEM via syslog.
[05:42] Priya: we require SAML-based SSO. is the Admin console compatible?
[05:45] Raj: yes — SAML and OIDC both supported, RBAC with SCIM provisioning.
[05:52] Luis: small practical — during local dev how do we simulate streaming?
[05:56] Raj: use the sandbox key and the local quickstart; streaming is identical in sandbox. we also include an envoy sidecar example for local replay.
[06:08] Maria: (no such attendee, background noise)
[06:12] Tom: about perf — can you explain batching strategy? we've seen variable latencies when batching too aggressively.
[06:18] Raj: sure — Redwood does continuous batching with an adaptive window based on target latency. you can set per-route SLOs and max-batch-size. Optimize suggests optimal windows based on your token distribution. sometimes the docs say baching, that's a typo.
[06:35] Priya: and token accounting — do you bill for prompt + completion tokens as one bucket?
[06:40] Maya: yes, usage billing is per-token generated + prompt tokens; Console gives per-route breakdown.
[06:47] Anika: the POC — we want to validate P50 < 120ms for short queries and P95 < 500ms for our medium workload. is that feasible?
[06:57] Raj: depends on model/quantization and Dedicated sizing. we can propose a Dedicated config, but hosted with low-latency models can hit P50 ~80-120ms for short prompts. we'll surface exact numbers in the perf checklist.
[07:12] Maya: moving to security — do you need SOC2 docs today?
[07:16] Anika: we need SOC2 and ISO attestation and a sample security architecture diagram.
[07:21] Maya: i'll attach SOC2 report and a redwood infra diagram — note: some transcriptions of product names in our docs are off, ignore typos.
[07:30] Raj: quick demo of Optimize recommendations — clicking into a route shows suggested batch windows, cache TTLs, and quantization candidates. for example, the route with lots of short prompts got a suggested prefix caching rule and a small batch window to keep P50 low.
[07:48] Tom: can you export those suggestions to a playbook?
[07:51] Raj: yes — export as a JSON plan or apply automatically as a rule, but we recommend manual review for safety.
[07:59] Priya: on encryption — in transit and at rest, and KMS for key control — fine, but what about HSM?
[08:07] Raj: we support customer-managed keys backed by HSM providers in private deployments. hosted can integrate with customer KMS too, it just depends on contract.
[08:18] Anika: curious about cost modeling — we need to present numbers to finance.
[08:24] Maya: we'll send a unit cost model: tokens per request, average token length, plus Dedicated node pricing. Also include burst pricing assumptions.
[08:34] Luis: random question — do you have rate limiting at the token or request level?
[08:38] Raj: both. per-key rate limits and token quotas. quota alerts in Console.
[08:44] Tom: ok let's try an end-to-end demo — Raj, can you run a small local script that calls the sandbox, then show the Console log and the optimize suggestion?
[08:53] Raj: doing that now — running the ts quickstart, sending 50 short prompts in a loop.
[09:05] (typing, deploy noise)
[09:18] Raj: request batch went through, see entries in the Console live tail, latency histogram popping up. you can click a sample trace to see where time was spent — network vs kernel vs decode.
[09:35] Priya: nice, that trace view will help us validate bottlenecks.
[09:40] Anika: during the POC can we run redwood-side profiling alongside our load generator? we want to capture P95 under sustained load.
[09:48] Raj: yes, we'll provide a perf harness — Raj to send the harness and a suggested load pattern.
[09:55] Maya: recap time — ask if any other compliance blockers.
[09:59] Anika: nothing else right now besides SOC2, SAML, KMS and data residency for EU traffic.
[10:08] Maya: noted — action items: we'll share SOC2, security diagram, sandbox keys, perf checklist.
[10:14] Tom: for timeline — we'd like a 4-week POC starting week of Oct 27, if possible.
[10:20] Maya: that works — we'll pencil it in but need your sample payloads and target SLAs.
[10:26] Anika: we'll share payloads by the 27th.
[10:30] Raj: a few technical clarifications i wanted to record — about model pinning: you can pin a model version per route, and run a canary with automatic fallback. there are also per-route timeouts and quota overrides.
[10:46] Priya: when you talk about fallback to quantized models, is there an automated metric to control it, like queue length or CPU usage?
[10:53] Raj: yes you can tie routing policy to metrics — latency, queue depth, region capacity. fallback is policy-driven. we'll include config examples.
[11:07] Luis: question — are embeddings handled in same SDK? we use embeddings for search.
[11:12] Raj: embeddings are part of the API and the SDK has a dedicated client method. we also have caching for embeddings with TTL.
[11:20] Tom: ok, last thing — demo artifacts. can you share the repo and a short runbook we can point engineers to?
[11:26] Maya: yes — sandbox repo link and runbook will be shared.
[11:31] Anika: thanks, this was very helpful.
[11:34] Maya: great — next steps recap: Maya shares links + SOC2 + infra diagram by 10/22; Raj shares perf harness and checklist by 10/22; Voltstream to send sample payloads and SLA targets by 10/27; schedule POC kickoff week of 10/27.
[11:56] (small chatter)
[12:02] Tom: we'll invite Sarah from security to the kickoff.
[12:07] Maya: perfect, we'll prepare a POC runbook. thanks everyone — we'll follow up in email.
[12:12] Anika: bye all.
[12:15] Meeting ended. Note: some transcribed words may be slightly off (product names, short terms), there were a couple of quiet lines accidentally tagged as other speakers.
